solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aunt boils muddy washing

indicators.note: something muddied is churned up and confused, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt boils dirty laundry clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddy' asks for the letters of AUNT BOILS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablutions is a formal or jocular word for the act of washing oneself.

clue.text: A bit aloof?

parts.note: a part is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: A query whether someone is slightly standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing apart keeps their distance, as an aloof person does.

clue.text: Promiscuous girl in fleece, one out of control?

parts.note: loose is an old word for sexually promiscuous

indicators.note: the girl goes in the swindle word

parts.note: to con is to swindle, or fleece
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wanton girl in a woolly jacket, perhaps wild and unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a garment but is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cannon is an unpredictable person who may cause harm, someone not under control.

clue.text: One's for skipping execution?

definitions.meaning: a rope is used for skipping games
... is the hangman's noose, execution by hanging

explanation.definitionFit: The rope means death by hanging, while a rope is also a child's skipping toy.

clue.text: Plant almost mature by Resurrection time

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: old means advanced in years
Easter celebrates Christ's resurrection

explanation.surface: A plant nearly fully grown in time for Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the D from OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a shrub, the wild olive or Russian olive.

clue.text: With drugs around, posh chap exploded

indicators.note: turned around, the drug letters run backwards

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so ES are ecstasy tablets
a toff is an upper-class man

explanation.surface: A rich man surrounded by narcotics flew into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the drug letters before the toff is added; 'exploded' is a past tense, as in a bomb that was set off.
explanation.definitionFit: Set off means detonated, as a bomb that has been set off has exploded.

clue.text: Stupid way Cymbeline ends?

definitions.meaning: the play's title finishes with its final letter, a vowel, described in three short words

explanation.surface: A jibe that Shakespeare's Cymbeline has a foolish ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN AN E: the name Cymbeline ends in an E. The question mark flags the wordplay sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes something silly or senseless, a close synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Duck swimmer secretly shows off

indicators.note: shows off says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A swimmer quietly showing off in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows off' signals the run of letters inside 'swimmer secretly'; 'Duck' is the verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water, to immerse them.

clue.text: Sailor's behind, a pink one?

parts.note: the Financial Times, FT, is printed on pink paper

explanation.surface: A sailor's rear, perhaps sunburnt pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a London business daily on salmon-pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical word for at or towards the stern, the back of a ship.

clue.text: Ran nude around church, showing stamina

indicators.note: letters messed around are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone streaked round a church, proving their staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but is the anagram indicator; the church abbreviation simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going, which is what stamina means.

clue.text: The right time to repent?

parts.note: read as two words, the answer names a precise clock time, an hour just after noon

explanation.surface: A question whether now is the proper moment to show remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AT ONE, a time of day; the question mark admits the looseness of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends for a wrong, which goes with repentance.

clue.text: Team's diet needs shaking up, it's thought

indicators.note: shaking something up disturbs its order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone reckons the team's eating plan needs an overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs shaking up' asks for the letters of TEAMS DIET to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimated means judged or reckoned, so a figure that is estimated is one that is thought to be so.

clue.text: Drunk, adversely affected by sport

parts.note: to be 'the worse for' something is to have suffered from it
to sport a garment is to wear it

explanation.surface: Someone who has been knocked about by playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is a verb here, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The worse for wear is an idiom for intoxicated as well as for battered or tired.

clue.text: Fascinating all-nighter, breaking up around noon

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the letter for noon
the word breaks into pieces that are reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A gripping party that went on all night, ending at about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' jumbles ALLNIGHTER; 'around' wraps those letters round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthralling means captivating, holding someone's attention completely.

clue.text: Couple allowed to form band

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Two people are permitted to start a music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical but is a ring worn on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn round the wrist.

clue.text: Witness Her Majesty supporting Times point of view

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as two by three
a stand is a position taken on an issue
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen's monogram

explanation.surface: The Queen is called to testify in favour of The Times newspaper's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is the multiplication word, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander sees an event without taking part, so is a witness.

clue.text: Gravedigger has lewd message being broadcast

parts.note: a sext is a sexually explicit text message
a programme being broadcast is on air, or on

explanation.surface: A cemetery worker has had his saucy text read out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer whose duties traditionally included digging graves.

clue.text: Female auditor a little frightening

parts.note: an auditor is a listener, and the ear is what listens
some means a certain amount

explanation.surface: A woman auditing the books is somewhat scary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means inspiring fear, which is frightening.

clue.text: Small group welcoming learner, naturally bright

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: a group that welcomes someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A small class takes in a student who is clever by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naturally bright' reads like brainy but means lit by daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlit means lit by the sun, bright in the natural way rather than by lamps.

clue.text: Look at cricket perhaps, quietly absorbed

indicators.note: the soft letter is soaked up inside the other word

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A spectator quietly engrossed in watching a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' is the chirping creature, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to look at carefully.

clue.text: Nice policeman?

parts.note: Nice is the French Riviera city, so its policeman is French, not merely pleasant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' reads as friendly, but capitalised at the start it hides the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police force, as found in Nice.

clue.text: Suspect friend heading north has debt notices

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards

parts.note: bud is short for buddy, a friend
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A dodgy pal moving north has bills piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns BUD into DUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious means doubtful or questionable, as a suspect claim is.

clue.text: Painter inspired by cooks making fish

indicators.note: breathed in by the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, so cooks gives two DOs
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword painter

explanation.surface: An artist takes his cue from chefs preparing seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' gives DO twice; 'do' for cook is unusual but matches 'done' for cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The dorado is a large golden game fish of warm seas, also called the mahi-mahi.

clue.text: Unfortunate year for the classically inclined?

definitions.text: Unfortunate year for the classically inclined?

parts.words: Unfortunate year for the classically inclined
parts.note: someone fond of the classics would describe a bad year in Latin

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase became famous when the Queen used it of 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means horrible year, a dreadful twelve months as a classicist would put it.

clue.text: Constituency wife held for Labour

indicators.note: the seat holds the letter within it

parts.note: a parliamentary seat is a constituency

explanation.surface: A constituency's MP's wife retained the seat for the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but means hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat means hard toil, as in by the sweat of your brow, which is labour.

clue.text: For Poirot, some trouble following each villain

indicators.note: one piece comes after another in the answer

parts.note: Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian detective, so 'some' in French: des
per means for each, as in a pound per head
ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Poirot has a little difficulty with every criminal he chases.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a villain of the Wild West kind.

clue.text: Quarrel noisily in Baden-Baden?

indicators.note: noisily means the word is said out loud, heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to argue or quarrel

explanation.surface: A loud row in a German resort town.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAR and SPA sound alike in British speech, which drops the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Baden is a German town famed for its thermal baths, an example of a spa.

clue.text: Woman with next to nothing as it happens

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
a broadcast shown as it happens is live

explanation.surface: A woman who, as luck would have it, owns almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Criticise rubbish written about case for Arkansas

indicators.note: one piece is written around another, so it goes inside

parts.note: rot means nonsense

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone slates a load of nonsense penned about the state of Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' takes just the outer letters of Arkansas; 'written about' puts them inside the word for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them harshly, an informal sense.

clue.text: Error in commentator's position on left

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: food left is left over

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so the word comes as it would be said aloud

parts.note: a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: A mistake in where a broadcaster has been seated on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commentator's' signals the sound: SITE, heard as SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something.
